main_deity: Originally Akṣobhya, now an image of donor
description_en: This small courtyard, known as Ikhālakhu Bāhāḥ, is located to the east of Ikhālakhucoka. The courtyard is behind a row of residential buildings near theIkhālakhu Jahru. It is paved with stone flooring.This small courtyard is located to the east ofIkhālakhuand can be reached through a narrow alley. Measuring 6.5m x 3.75m, it consists of a raised plinth on the northern wall containing three small statues with stone roofs, atop of which are small stupas. At the center is aśikharakūṭa caityawith a base measuring 140 x 140 cm and a height of 170 cm. A dharmadhātu maṇḍala(90 cm tall) adjoins it on its northern side. A smallcaitya(70cm tall) can be found on the southern plinth attached to the building, and appears to be in a neglected state. A bell hangs on two stone pillars (13 x 13 cm and 170 cm high) to the east of the courtyard.This tiny courtyard reaches the minimum requirements for a Bāhāḥ as defined by Locke. Bruce Owens notes that thekwāḥpāḥ dyaḥ,caitya, and other features are under threat as this space has been used to store lumber (and now detritus from the reconstruction) since at least 2008. Indeed, most of the features generally found in avihāracannot be found here. There is, for instance, no god-house (dyaḥchẽ). Local people therefore consider this place to just be acokarather than avihāra.Three south-facing and connected shrines house the main deities of thevihāra.WhenLocke(1985, 140) studied this place, there was an image of Akṣobhya inside the middle shrine, an image of Prajñāpāramitā inside the shrine right to it and an image of Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara inside the left shrine, however these images have since been stolen. In their place, statues of a doner in the act of praying have been installed inside the middle shrine, whilst the right-hand shirine now contains an image of Lakṣmī holding a lotus flower in her hand. The left-hand shrine has been furnished with an image of a two-handed Lokeśvara holding a lotus in his left hand and with his right hand in avaradagesture. Above the middle and the left shrine, one can find images of Mahākāla and three doners. These have been placed in a disorganized way. Local people claim that this Bāhāḥwas made by Śreṣṭhas. Apart from this, nothing more is known about its history.Inside the courtyard, there is oneśikharakūṭa caityaand adharmadhātu maṇḍala. At the eastern corner of the courtyard is a bell that was donated in NS 1049, and at the southern corner one can find another smallcaitya. Note that the illustration identified by Locke (1985, 141I) as Ikhalakhu Baha is actually Iku Baha, and the photograph of Ikhalaku (mis-labeled as Iku Baha) is actually on p. 139.
description_ne: इखालखु चोकको पूर्वपट्टि इखालखु बाहा:  नामको सानो चोक छ । इखालखु जह्रुको नजिकै व्यक्तिगत घरहरुको पछाडि यो चोक रहेको छ । चोकमा ढुङ्गा बिछ्याइएको छ । एउटा विहारमा सामान्यतया हुनुपर्ने विशेषताहरू यसमा पाइँदैनन् । विहारमा द्य:छेँ छैन । त्यसकारण स्थानीयहरू यस स्थानलाई विहारको रूपमा नलिएर चोकको रूपमा पनि लिने गर्दछन् । विहारको मूल देवताको रूपमा दक्षिणाभिमुख तीनवटा देवस्थानहरू टाँस्सिएर रहेका छन् । लक (१९८५, १४०) ले अध्ययन गर्दा बीचमा रहेको देवस्थानमा अक्षोभ्यको मूर्ति, दायाँतर्फकोमा प्रज्ञापारमिता र बायाँतर्फकोमा षडक्षरी लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति राखिएका थिए, तर ती मूर्तिहरू चोरी भइसकेकोले अहिले बीचको देवस्थानमा कुनै दाताको नमस्कार गरिरहेको मूर्ति,  दायाँपट्टिकोमा हातमा कमलको फूल लिएकी लक्ष्मीको मूर्ति र बायाँपट्टिकोमा दुई हात भएका देब्रे हातले कमलको फूल लिएका र दायाँ हात वरद मुद्रामा रहेका लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति राखिएको छ । तीनै वटा देवस्थानको माथि गजूरको रूपमा ससाना चैत्य राखिएको छ । बीचको र बायाँपट्टिको देवस्थानको माथि  अव्यवस्थित ढंगले महाकाल र दाताको प्रतिमा राखिएका छन् । चोकमा एउटा शिखरकूट चैत्य र एउटा धर्मधातु मण्डल रहेका छन् । चोकको पूर्वी भागमा नेसं १०४९ मा स्थापना गरिएको घण्टा रहेको छ भने दक्षिणतिरको पेटीमा अर्को सानो चैत्य रहेको छ । यो विहार श्रेष्ठहरूले बनाएका थिए, तर विहारको ऐतिहासिकताका बारे थप केही थाहा हुन सकेन । निकै उपेक्षित अवस्थामा रहेको यो विहार बिग्रेका सामान थुपार्ने ठाउँ बनेको छ, यस चोकको राम्रो व्यवस्थापन हुन सकेको छैन ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: Śilpakāra Muni Rāja, his elder son Kṛṣṇa Rāja and family made thisdharmadhātu maṇḍala.
Śilpakāra Sukha Bhāju and his wife Rāj Māyā donated this bell.
